title: Real KaTeX glyph compositor experiment

sourceRefs.summary: Run-contract target that explains why this generated contract exists.
Human-approved 24-slice proposal, preservation boundary, complexity budget, visual checkpoint, and stop conditions.

allowedWork: Slices 1-12 may build one isolated real-KaTeX solve-x compositor exemplar using the existing material layer, computed-style clone, font readiness, semantic motion selectors, lineage matcher, and bounded scheduler.
Slices 13-24 remain gated until explicit human promotion after slice 12, then may generalize the same compositor to fraction merge, plus-minus split, and one crowded responsive case.
Add at most four focused compositor production modules and six generic lifecycle primitives; commit and verify each slice independently.
disallowedWork: No operation-, fraction-, quadratic-, branch-, or viewport-specific scheduler; no durable DOM, glyph geometry, keyframes, or backend plans; clones never own accessibility or interaction.
No radical repair, family rollout, Manim implementation, Python runtime, video encoding, CAS, live LLM API, new renderer family, curriculum expansion, or unrelated user work.
goal: Determine whether actual rendered KaTeX fragments can produce convincing object-constant solve-x motion and, only after human promotion, generalize through one semantic-constrained compositor.
commitCadence: Commit each slice only with its verification and completed Theseus evidence.
stopConditions: Stop if semantic selectors require undocumented KaTeX-tree guessing.
Stop if solve-x still requires whole-equation fading or mid-flight character replacement.
Stop if one bounded shared geometry or handoff correction cannot eliminate the visible native-settlement jump.
Stop if any case requires operation-, fraction-, quadratic-, branch-, or viewport-specific scheduling.
Stop if DOM nodes, measurements, keyframes, or backend plans enter the durable artifact or moving clones own accessibility or interaction.
Stop if more than four compositor production modules or six lifecycle primitives are required, or performance requires case-specific optimization.
Stop on semantic, reader, branching, Cloze, production-closure, radical, scope, or unrelated-user-work regression.
Stop at slice 12 for explicit human promotion; do not execute slices 13-24 on initial approval.
Stop if the slice-12 exemplar still reads as a crossfade, ghost, or text substitution.

slices.title: Failed-overlay-baseline
slices.summary: Froze four observed overlay failure codes, six real-glyph acceptance laws, a one-pixel handoff tolerance, and fixed module/lifecycle complexity budgets.

slices.title: Durable-boundary-ratchet
slices.summary: Ratchet-tested the durable artifact boundary against five classes of ephemeral compositor state.

slices.title: Fragment-observation-contract
slices.summary: Added the ephemeral native KaTeX fragment observation contract with exact identity, geometry, style, and font-revision validation.

slices.title: Semantic-KaTeX-leaf-observation
slices.summary: Observed exact explicitly tagged KaTeX fragment subtrees with stage-relative bounds and computed-style fingerprints; ambiguous nodes fail closed.

slices.title: Coordinate-normalization
slices.summary: Normalized browser fragment rectangles into stable local CSS coordinates across transformed and responsive stages.

slices.title: Font-and-style-settlement
slices.summary: Native fragment observation now waits for fonts and rejects computed-style or greater-than-quarter-pixel geometry drift across consecutive layout frames.

slices.title: Lineage-fragment-binding
slices.summary: Native source and target fragments now bind only inside canonical semantic lineage; unrelated equal glyphs fail closed.

slices.title: Computed-style-fragment-clone
slices.summary: Exact observed KaTeX subtrees can now be cloned into the existing material layer with computed typography and no accessibility, focus, hover, or semantic authority.

slices.title: Exclusive-visual-ownership
slices.summary: Source native, inert clone transit, and target native now exchange visual authority atomically with no crossfade or double-rendered glyph.

slices.title: Exact-native-handoff
slices.summary: The real KaTeX clone now follows one generic native-rectangle interpolation and reaches an exact, typography-matched atomic target handoff within the one-pixel acceptance bound.

slices.title: Gradual-context-reflow
slices.summary: Persistent context now reflows continuously toward target geometry while local departing context clears independently, with no whole-equation or persistent-context opacity change.
